note: The Phase 0 font registry (decisions.md D-29, PRD §10.8.4, tech-spec §11). Fonts are referenced from a RenderManifest by sha256, NEVER by family name: a name is a request the system resolves however it likes, and a resolver that silently substitutes a fallback breaks both determinism and the rights record at once. The renderer verifies each file against the hash below and REFUSES the render on a mismatch rather than substituting. Source: Inter v4.1 (https://github.com/rsms/inter/releases/tag/v4.1), static TTFs from `extras/ttf/`. Static rather than the variable `InterVariable.ttf` because libass's variable-font support is partial and an instance it cannot resolve renders at a default weight without saying so — a silent visual change is exactly what hashing is meant to prevent.

licence.name: SIL Open Font License 1.1
licence.note: The OFL permits commercial embedding and redistribution as part of a product. A BRAND font is a different matter: StyleProfile fonts carry `rightsRecorded`, and a brand font with no recorded commercial grant must not be added here (PRD §10.8.4).

fonts.why: SemiBold, not Regular. Open captions sit over moving video with no guaranteed contrast behind them; Regular loses legibility against a bright frame at the sizes REQ-084's readability rules allow.

libassFontsDirNote: libass loads EVERY file in its fontsdir and errors on anything that is not a font, so the font FILES live alone in this subdirectory while the registry and licence stay in the parent. Verified against ffmpeg 8.0.1: pointing fontsdir at data/fonts produced "Error opening memory font fonts.json".
